court: Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction finality
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction to review the final judgment and remedial injunction.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply de novo review for summary judgment and appropriate review for standing, mootness, and injunctive relief.

issues.label: Proper defendant substitution
issues.why: The court must ensure the official-capacity defendant was properly substituted under Rule 25(d).

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment constraints
issues.why: The court must determine whether Ex parte Young permits the requested prospective relief against a state official.

issues.label: Ex parte Young scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether the injunction is truly prospective and not effectively compensatory or retroactive.

issues.label: Sovereign immunity for federal statutes
issues.why: The court must assess whether any federal statutory claims are barred or limited by sovereign immunity absent valid abrogation or waiver.

issues.label: Article III injury-in-fact (individuals)
issues.why: The court must decide whether each individual plaintiff suffered a concrete, particularized injury from DSS practices.

issues.label: Article III injury-in-fact (organization)
issues.why: The court must determine whether Empower Missouri suffered a cognizable diversion-of-resources or other injury.

issues.label: Causation (traceability)
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs’ injuries are fairly traceable to Bax’s challenged policies/practices.

issues.label: Redressability
issues.why: The court must determine whether declaratory/injunctive relief against Bax would likely redress each injury.

issues.label: Prospective harm likelihood
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether future injury is sufficiently imminent (recertification cycles, ongoing practices).

issues.label: Standing for each claim
issues.why: The court must ensure plaintiffs have standing separately for SNAP Act, due process, and ADA theories.

issues.label: Standing for each remedy
issues.why: The court must ensure plaintiffs have standing for the specific declaratory and operational injunction components sought.

issues.label: Mootness by benefit approval
issues.why: The court must decide whether later approval of benefits moots individual claims.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation doctrine
issues.why: The court must assess whether DSS’s post-suit actions make recurrence unlikely enough to moot the case.

issues.label: Capable-of-repetition exception
issues.why: The court must consider whether recurring recertification/administration issues evade review and may recur.

issues.label: Organizational claim mootness
issues.why: The court must determine whether Empower Missouri’s alleged ongoing diversion persists despite current approvals.

issues.label: Ripeness of forward-looking relief
issues.why: The court must decide whether requested systemic injunction is ripe or based on speculative future events.

issues.label: Political question/justiciability
issues.why: The court must consider whether the requested operational mandates are judicially manageable and appropriate for courts.

issues.label: Plaintiffs’ property interest
issues.why: The court must determine whether applicants/recipients have a protected property interest in SNAP benefits at application and recertification stages.

issues.label: Eligibility vs entitlement nuance
issues.why: The court must distinguish property interests of applicants versus current recipients in continued benefits.

issues.label: State action requirement
issues.why: The court must confirm DSS administration constitutes state action for Fourteenth Amendment due process claims.

issues.label: Procedural due process framework
issues.why: The court must apply Mathews v. Eldridge balancing to identify required procedures.

issues.label: Adequacy of interview opportunity
issues.why: The court must decide whether DSS provided a meaningful opportunity to complete interviews before denial.

issues.label: Notice sufficiency
issues.why: The court must assess whether applicants received constitutionally adequate notice of requirements and consequences.

issues.label: Hearing/appeal availability
issues.why: The court must consider whether existing administrative review cures alleged due process deficiencies.

issues.label: Arbitrary administration theory
issues.why: The court must decide whether inconsistent processes amount to arbitrary deprivation under due process.

issues.label: Causation of denial (Holmes)
issues.why: The court must determine whether denial resulted from DSS policy (automatic denial) versus applicant noncompliance.

issues.label: Causation of denial (Davis)
issues.why: The court must resolve factual/legal significance of the unregistered application and alleged wrong SSN.

issues.label: Recertification handling (Dallas)
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS’s recertification process and assistance obligations were violated.

issues.label: Meaningful access concept
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS processes denied meaningful access to benefits, relevant to due process and ADA.

issues.label: SNAP Act private right of action
issues.why: The court must decide whether 7 U.S.C. §§ 2014/2020 and regulations are enforceable by private plaintiffs.

issues.label: Section 1983 enforceability
issues.why: The court must decide whether SNAP provisions create rights enforceable under 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

issues.label: Implied right analysis
issues.why: If not via §1983, the court must determine whether Congress implied a private right and remedy in SNAP.

issues.label: Supremacy/Preemption claim viability
issues.why: The court must consider whether plaintiffs may seek injunctive relief to stop state practices contrary to federal law absent a private right.

issues.label: Federal regulation enforceability
issues.why: The court must determine whether accompanying SNAP regulations create enforceable rights or only guide agency discretion.

issues.label: Interpretation of §2020(e)(2)(B)
issues.why: The court must construe the ‘first day of contact’ and prompt processing obligations and their scope.

issues.label: Interpretation of interview rules
issues.why: The court must determine what federal law requires regarding interview scheduling and completion for applications/recertifications.

issues.label: Legality of automatic denial rule
issues.why: The court must decide whether denying all non-interviewed applications after 30 days regardless of applicant effort violates federal law or due process.

issues.label: Effect of alleged waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether any federal waiver exists, its terms, and whether it affects obligations at recertification.

issues.label: Waiver evidentiary record
issues.why: The court must address whether the missing waiver document precludes summary judgment or requires additional proof.

issues.label: Administrative exhaustion
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs were required to pursue state administrative appeals before suing (for statutory or constitutional claims).

issues.label: Primary jurisdiction/deference
issues.why: The court must consider whether federal agency interpretations (USDA/FNS) warrant deference on SNAP administration requirements.

issues.label: Due process remedy tailoring
issues.why: The court must ensure any due process injunction remedies the procedural violation without overreaching.

issues.label: ADA Title II applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS is a public entity and Bax’s official-capacity suit properly invokes Title II.

issues.label: ADA standing (Holmes)
issues.why: The court must determine whether Holmes is a qualified individual with a disability and suffered discrimination by reason of disability.

issues.label: ADA standing (Dallas)
issues.why: The court must determine whether Dallas is a qualified individual with a disability and suffered denial of meaningful access.

issues.label: Qualified individual definition
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs meet essential eligibility requirements for SNAP with or without reasonable modifications.

issues.label: Disability knowledge/notice
issues.why: The court must assess whether DSS had sufficient notice of disability and need for accommodation, especially for Dallas’s note.

issues.label: Reasonable accommodation duty
issues.why: The court must decide what modifications were required (assistance, alternative communication, in-person interview, simplified prompts).

issues.label: Reasonableness and undue burden
issues.why: The court must consider whether requested accommodations are reasonable or would fundamentally alter SNAP administration or impose undue burdens.

issues.label: Causation under ADA
issues.why: The court must decide whether any denial/delay occurred because of disability versus general call-center congestion.

issues.label: Disparate impact vs intentional discrimination
issues.why: The court must determine the required showing for Title II injunctive relief (and whether intent matters here).

issues.label: Integration with Section 504
issues.why: The court must consider whether Section 504 obligations apply and whether they are properly in the case/relief.

issues.label: ADA grievance procedure requirement
issues.why: The court must determine whether Title II regulations require DSS to adopt grievance procedures and whether enforceable by plaintiffs.

issues.label: Scope of declaratory relief
issues.why: The court must determine whether requested declarations are sufficiently concrete and tied to live disputes.

issues.label: Permanent injunction prerequisites
issues.why: The court must assess actual success on merits, irreparable harm, balance of equities, and public interest.

issues.label: Irreparable harm showing
issues.why: The court must determine whether plaintiffs showed likely ongoing harm absent injunction despite current benefit receipt.

issues.label: Equitable discretion limits
issues.why: The court must ensure the court did not abuse discretion by imposing operational mandates beyond legal violations.

issues.label: Rule 65 specificity
issues.why: The injunction must state terms specifically and describe required acts in reasonable detail.

issues.label: Injunction overbreadth
issues.why: The court must decide whether statewide systemic relief exceeds what is necessary to redress plaintiffs’ injuries.

issues.label: Nexus to plaintiffs’ injuries
issues.why: Each operational requirement (wait times, denial-rate caps, staffing) must be tied to remedying proven legal violations.

issues.label: Federalism/comity concerns
issues.why: The court must consider limits on federal courts managing state agencies, especially detailed performance metrics.

issues.label: PLRA inapplicability check
issues.why: The court must confirm whether any statute limiting institutional reform injunctions applies (and if not, why).

issues.label: Ongoing judicial supervision
issues.why: The court must assess whether the reporting requirements and continuing oversight are permissible equitable relief.

issues.label: Separation-of-powers within state
issues.why: The court must consider whether ordering reports to state legislators/executives improperly intrudes into state governance.

issues.label: Modification of resource centers
issues.why: The court must decide whether ordering maintenance of in-person operations is legally required under SNAP/ADA and supported by record.

issues.label: Prohibition on operational changes
issues.why: The court must assess legality of enjoining facility hours/staffing changes pending statewide policies.

issues.label: Performance benchmarks legality
issues.why: The court must decide whether mandating 90% calls under 20 minutes and denial caps is authorized and supported.

issues.label: Summary judgment factual disputes
issues.why: The court must determine whether genuine disputes exist (e.g., application registration, waiver existence, causation) precluding summary judgment.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency
issues.why: The court must verify admissibility and sufficiency of declarations, records, and statistics supporting systemic findings.

issues.label: Classwide relief without class
issues.why: The court must consider whether granting broad statewide relief to nonparties is permissible absent class certification.

issues.label: Scope of relief vs claims
issues.why: The court must ensure the remedial order addresses only claims actually adjudicated (due process/ADA vs SNAP Act).

issues.label: Unadjudicated SNAP Act claims
issues.why: The court must decide whether the district court relied on SNAP Act compliance despite not resolving private right questions.

issues.label: Cumulative remedies and duplication
issues.why: The court must ensure remedies under due process and ADA are not duplicative or inconsistent and are properly grounded.

issues.label: Attorneys’ fees eligibility
issues.why: If sought, the court must consider prevailing-party status and statutory basis (e.g., §1988, ADA fee provision).

issues.label: Relief against official capacity only
issues.why: The court must ensure relief runs against the office (policy/practice) and not impose improper personal obligations.

issues.label: Continuing jurisdiction basis
issues.why: The court must determine whether retaining jurisdiction to monitor compliance is justified and properly limited.

issues.label: Remand instructions scope
issues.why: If reversing or narrowing, the court must decide what issues require fact-finding or tailored relief on remand.
